title: Janaka's bow
hook: a bow no king could lift, picked up as if it were nothing, and the sound that follows

segments.voice: Yesterday: Janaka's bow, part two. Strength as the bride-price, a city besieged by kings who failed, and a cart hauled by thousands. Did you let an urge to blame the test pass? Day five hundred nine.

The chest is open. The bow lies there, enormous. Nobody in the hall speaks. Vishvamitra looks at Rama and says one short line: Rama, my son, look at the bow. That's all. No speech. Rama steps forward and asks, politely: may I touch it? May I try to lift it, and string it? The king and the sage both say yes. And then, in front of thousands of people, something happens that Valmiki tells in only a few verses.
screen: `THE CHEST IS OPEN.` → `RAMA, MY SON, LOOK AT THE BOW.` → `MAY I TOUCH IT?`

segments.voice: Rama takes hold of the bow in the middle and lifts it, the text says, as if in play. The bow that thousands of men just dragged in on a cart, and that a line of kings couldn't budge. He bends it and strings it. And then he draws the string back, all the way to his ear. And with a crack like thunder, the bow breaks in two. The sound is enormous. The earth shakes like a mountain splitting. Everyone in the hall falls to the ground, stunned, everyone except four: Vishvamitra, King Janaka, Rama and Lakshmana. Notice a few things. Rama asks permission before touching it. He doesn't grab at it the way the angry kings would have. He lifts it lightly, which tells you the strength isn't a strain for him. And he doesn't set out to break it; he draws it fully, the way a bow is meant to be drawn, and it can't hold him. Notice too who stays standing. The teacher, the father, the one who drew it, and the brother who never leaves his side. When the people come to, Janaka speaks, and his words are full of joy. I've seen Rama's strength with my own eyes. Sita will bring glory to our family by marrying him. My promise is fulfilled. And he asks Vishvamitra's leave to send fast messengers to Ayodhya, to bring Dasharatha. The bow is broken. The wedding is coming.
screen: `MAY I TOUCH IT? HE ASKS FIRST.` · `LIFTED AS IF IN PLAY.` · `DRAWN TO THE EAR, IT BREAKS.` · `FOUR STILL STANDING.` · then, large: `THE BOW BREAKS IN TWO.`

segments.voice: Sit and settle. Imagine picking up something heavy you've been carrying for a long time, a worry, a task, a grudge, and finding it lighter than you thought, as if in play. Breathe in, and lift it. Breathe out, and set it down. Don't force anything. Just let the breath show you how light it could be. The bell holds the time.
Janaka's bow. Rama asks to touch it, lifts it as if in play, strings it, and draws it until it breaks with a crack like thunder.
Your line: Janaka's bow. Today, before you pick up something that isn't yours, a tool, a phone, a task, ask first, the way Rama did. Day five hundred nine.

howItsDone: The breaking of the bow is a high point of Ramlila performances and Ramayana recitations; in many places audiences cheer as the bow snaps, and the scene is often painted and sung at weddings.

fork.setup: you're Rama. the sage says, look at the bow. the whole hall is watching. what do you do?
options: grab it and lift it at once.
ask permission to touch it and try.
fork.reveal: he asks if he may touch it, lift it and string it. given leave, he lifts it as if in play, and it breaks.

original.note: Sanskrit dhanus: a bow. the root of dhanur-veda, the art of archery.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama proves he's strongest by snapping a bow.
what it means: he asks first, lifts it lightly, draws it as a bow is drawn, and it can't hold him.
what a scholar hears: Bala Kanda 67 tells it in a few verses: lifted lila-iva, as if in play; drawn to the ear; broken in the middle with a sound like thunder; only four remain standing.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 67 (the bow lifted, strung and broken; Janaka's joy)

notes: 'Lila-iva' (as if in play) for how Rama lifts the bow: confirm the text's word.
The four who remain standing (Vishvamitra, Janaka, Rama, Lakshmana): confirm.
